page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 192.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-core throughput and strong vector calculation performance. The PassMark CPU test reached 104,787.21 points, placing it in the top 10%, complemented by an extended instructions score of 119,233.71. Geekbench multi-core achieved 18,336.0 points, while specific routines such as software compilation with Clang (58,511.0) and ray tracing (102,598.0) registered in the top 10%. Memory read bandwidth reached 333.72 GB/sec for large blocks and 7,017.2 GB/sec for small cached blocks, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 575.95 GB/sec.

Network serving and in-memory transactional tests also show high throughput, with static web serving reaching 142.01 GB/sec and Redis SET operations delivering 151.03 million operations per second. Machine learning prompt processing reached 304.72 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. The 2 GB per core ratio represents an optimized hardware density tradeoff that yields cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks, though workloads demanding extreme RAM allocations or low-latency local NVMe scratch space will need to account for the absence of local disks and the lower memory-per-core ratio.

Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as continuous integration, massive software build pipelines, batch data processing, ray tracing, web serving farms, and distributed network services.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-focused instance within the General Purpose family, powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores with hyperthreading), 480 MB of L3 cache, and 192.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The instance features vector acceleration extensions including AVX-512 and AMX, but does not provide onboard local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, scoring 104,787.21 in PassMark CPU, 58,511.0 in Clang software compilation, and delivering 151.03 million Redis SET operations per second. With large uncached read memory bandwidth of 333.72 GB/sec, it offers cost-efficient processing capacity where compute density takes precedence over large per-core memory reserves. It is best suited for CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, batch data transformation, and distributed analytics.
